correctness.rationale: All six possible characteristics follow from the Wendt resultant. For the four primes >26, g=13 divides p-1 so the product parameter lies in F_p, t≥6 permits both inverse-power-sum constraints, and 13j≤p makes them nonvacuous. Exact exhaustive modular computation rules out all possibilities, including both branches for four p=8191 roots. An exact F53 quotient permutation and an exact F27 extension-field permutation establish the other two primes. The verifier and the published lemmas cover all extension degrees.

broader_coverage.reasoning: In the coprime-index extension, gcd(d(Q-1),Q^e-1)=Q-1, so index 13 would require Q=14, which is not a prime power. Thus that broad-looking family has no index-thirteen member. The unrestricted finiteness theorem admits the six candidate primes but does not eliminate four.

value.rationale: The complete existence spectrum for the natural fixed index immediately beyond the studied index-eleven prime case is a motivated finite classification over all extension degrees. The result reduces a known six-prime Wendt necessary list to exactly two true characteristics, and the p=8191 case requires genuinely joint inverse-power-sum constraints. The known Wendt factorization alone gives none of these four nonexistence statements.
